topStories.headline: D8 Race Enters Final Stretch: Three Candidates Spar at Commonwealth Club Forum
topStories.dek: With eleven days until Election Day, McCoy, Nguyen, and Patel clashed Tuesday over housing, surveillance, and political endorsements — as Yekutiel's name lingers on the ballot.
topStories.body:
The race to succeed term-limited Supervisor Rafael Mandelman heated up Tuesday evening when the three remaining District 8 candidates — Gary McCoy, Michael Nguyen, and Darshini Patel — faced each other at a forum hosted by Commonwealth Club World Affairs and the San Francisco Democratic Party. The debate, billed as the Gr8T Debate, marked the sharpest public exchange yet in a contest covering the Castro, Noe Valley, Glen Park, Diamond Heights, and surrounding neighborhoods.

The session grew contentious quickly when McCoy and Nguyen pressed Patel over an unsolicited endorsement from centrist group GrowSF. Patel said she had declined the endorsement and never filled out a questionnaire for the group, telling the audience she spent more than ten minutes on the phone asking GrowSF to explain why it was backing her over her explicit objections. GrowSF proceeded regardless, running ads on her behalf.

On housing, all three candidates said they support denser development around the district's two Safeway sites. They diverged on rent control and Mayor Lurie's Family Zoning Plan: Nguyen opposed the plan while McCoy and Patel backed it. On public safety, Nguyen argued the mayor's administration has no real strategy for street disorder. McCoy pointed to endorsements from both SF YIMBY and the SF Tenants Union as evidence of his cross-aisle approach. Patel said the Board's role is to question the mayor's agenda because there is always room for improvement.

Manny Yekutiel, who withdrew from the race on October 1 following multiple sexual assault allegations, remains on the November 3 ballot. A poll commissioned by GrowSF shortly after his exit showed his support had collapsed, leaving a three-candidate race with McCoy currently holding the front-runner position. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3.

topStories.headline: Planning Wants Six New Landmark Districts in Duboce Triangle — Community Meetings Just Wrapped
topStories.dek: SF Planning and Supervisor Mandelman held back-to-back forums this week on a proposal to designate six collections of Victorian and Edwardian buildings as protected historic districts, with adoption targeted for December.
topStories.body:
Duboce Triangle residents got their first detailed look this week at a plan to significantly expand historic protections across the neighborhood. San Francisco Planning, joining Supervisor Rafael Mandelman, held an in-person community meeting on Wednesday, October 21, at the Gazebo Room of CPMC Davies Campus at 601 Castro Street, followed by a virtual session on Thursday evening.

The proposal calls for six new landmark districts within Duboce Triangle, covering buildings ranging from small groupings of just three structures to collections of roughly fifty. All of the targeted buildings were constructed between 1875 and 1913 and are described by Planning as architecturally significant residential collections. One of the six — a proposed district covering fifteen properties on Beaver Street — has been publicly identified so far, with outreach to affected property owners already underway.

The effort builds on Duboce Triangle's existing Duboce Park Landmark District, designated more than a decade ago, which covers nearly ninety residential buildings. The Duboce Triangle Neighborhood Association spent years surveying properties west of Noe Street and south of Duboce Avenue that fell outside the original survey boundary; the six new proposals grew from that community-funded work.

Landmark designation in San Francisco requires a public hearing at the Historic Preservation Commission, then a second public hearing and majority vote at the Board of Supervisors, followed by the mayor's signature. Planning staff said at this week's meetings that adoption of the new districts is targeted for December. Property owners within the proposed boundaries can request a one-on-one meeting with Planning staff through the department.

topStories.headline: Glen Park Station Bar Raised a Glass to 100 Years Last Weekend
topStories.dek: The village's longest-running drinking establishment marked a full century on October 17 with a street closure, an all-day party, and a history talk from the neighborhood's own archivist.
topStories.body:
Glen Park's Glen Park Station bar turned 100 years old this month, and the neighborhood turned out to celebrate. The centennial party ran Saturday, October 17, from 1 to 9 p.m. at 2816 Diamond Street, with a street closure along Diamond from 5 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. to give the festivities room to spread.

At 1:30 p.m., Evelyn Rose, founder of the Glen Park Neighborhoods History Project, led a public history talk tracing the bar's origins in 1926 and its hundred-year run as the neighborhood's social anchor. Rose has previously led presentations on Glen Park's transit and architectural history; the centennial talk extended that ongoing effort to document the village's past for residents and newcomers alike.

The bar came under new ownership earlier this decade when Glen Park residents Sean Kelly and Shane Ryan purchased both the business and the building, motivated in part by a desire to keep the institution from becoming something unrecognizable to longtime regulars. The centennial celebration was organized in partnership with the Glen Park Merchants Association. The Glen Park Association posted notice of the event on October 15 and called for volunteers to help staff the street closure barricades.

events.description: Glen Park Beautiful's Renee Berger co-leads a guided Walktober walk visiting five of the city's tiled staircases, finishing with a relaxed grand finale at Glen Park Station. Part of the citywide SF Stairway Month series.

events.title: Ives Collective Fall Concert

events.title: Noe Valley Night Market — October Edition
events.location: Noe Valley Town Square, 24th Street at Sanchez
events.description: Noe Valley Merchants host the monthly fall night market with live music, local food vendors, retail stalls, a bounce house, face painting, and balloon art. MC Lambert Moss leads the evening's musical lineup. The 48 Quintara/24th Street Muni route reroutes and 24th Street between Sanchez and Vicksburg closes from 2 to 10 p.m. Free to attend.

events.title: Halloween in the Castro: Block Party & Night Market
events.description: The Castro's annual Halloween celebration returns with four blocks of programming across three stages — trick-or-treating, a costume contest, live entertainment, local food vendors, and the neon-lit Glow in the Streets outdoor dance party. Free to attend; presented by CG Events and the Castro Merchants Association.

events.title: Haunted Chenery — Glen Park Halloween
events.location: Chenery Street between Diamond and Elk, Glen Park
events.description: Chenery Street closes to traffic for Glen Park's car-free trick-or-treat tradition. This year's pumpkin display from the Vella family on Sussex Street features 175 carved pumpkins glowing from dusk; neighbors can join the carving on October 28, 29, and 30. Organized by the Glen Park Association.

moreNews.headline: Hoodline Profiles Frenchie Wine Bar, the Natural-Wine Spot on the Noe Valley-Mission Border
moreNews.body: Hoodline ran a feature on October 22 on Frenchie Wine Bar at 1007 Guerrero Street, on the border of Noe Valley and the Mission. Co-founders Natalia Morarasu and Joel Arias named the bar after their French bulldog, Dolcetto — a nod to an Italian wine grape meaning little sweet one. Morarasu grew up on a grape-farming family in Moldova before spending nearly a decade in San Francisco hospitality; Arias previously served as wine director at Embarcadero restaurant La Mar Cocina Peruana. The bar pours more than sixty biodynamic and low-intervention wines alongside Peruvian-influenced small plates and welcomes dogs. Frenchie opened in 2025 in the former space of Turkish restaurant Tuba.

moreNews.headline: Glen Park Rec Center Small Field Closes Through November 23 for Turf Restoration
moreNews.body: The small field behind Glen Park Recreation Center closed Monday, October 19, for turf restoration work and is expected to remain out of service through Monday, November 23, according to a notice posted this week by the Glen Park Association. Residents looking for open play space in the area in the interim can use the recreation center's other facilities.
